newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Libya slams European rapid reaction force.
newsitem.headline: Libya slams European rapid reaction force.

text.p: Libya has denounced the formation of a rapid reaction force by four European countries as a threat to the independence of North African states.
El Jamahiria newspaper said the formation of the force known as Eurofor by France, Italy, Spain and Portugal on Saturday was a "declaration of war in the south Mediterranean".
Once fully operational, Eurofor will be able to call on up to 10,000 troops for use on humanitarian and peacekeeping missions. It has its command headquarters in Florence, Italy.

The Libyan news agency JANA said Libya's foreign minister, Omar Mustafa al-Montasser, summoned the four countries' ambassadors on Sunday evening and "informed them of the anxiety and unease of the Great Jamahiriyah (Libya)" about the agreement to set up the force.
Montasser said the agreement "could not be accepted in the 21st century" and asked for an explanation from the four governments through their ambassadors.
Libyan television said another cabinet member met diplomats from Algeria, Morocco and Tunisia on Sunday and stressed the importance of reaching a unified stance towards the force.

The secretary for unity affairs, Jomaa al-Fezzani, told the three diplomats that Libya "totally rejects it (Eurofor) because of the dangers it entails and which threaten the independence of the Arab Maghreb Union states". The union groups Algeria, Libya, Mauritania, Morocco and Tunisia.
El Jamahiria said formation of the force signalled "a new conflict between South and North" and showed that the European countries "make light of the dignity and freedom of others".
